_meta.note: MANAGER and OWNER both authenticate as GYM_OWNER; the split is a permission inside one partner account, not a separate role. Enforced server-side by gym-service partner-context.middleware.ts (requirePartnerOwner, requireGymScope); client-side checks are UX convenience only.

roles.note: an account can hold PT and also access full client capabilities via an activeView toggle; exact backend mechanism pending verification

roles.sub_permission: OWNER vs MANAGER, enforced in gym-service partner-context.middleware.ts, not a separate auth role

removed_roles.note: existed historically, removed per web AppContext.tsx comment citing 'Money-flow plan 5.1' — not the same concept as today's MANAGER permission

authorization_findings.finding: Admin role/status mutation routes have no in-service role check in auth-service, gateway-only enforcement
/auth/internal/* and other internal routes reachable through public gateway proxy, single shared static secret, non-constant-time comparison
No complete owner-check / cross-user-isolation test suite exists; authorization verified by sampling only
ai-service requireRole middleware trusts gateway-injected x-user-role headers by design, documented as conditional on ai-service not being publicly reachable
Coach(PT)-client relationship re-check on the server independently verified as real (not just claimed)
Shared unscoped exercise cache depends on every caller re-applying USER_CUSTOM visibility after read

PT-to-client authorization confirmed robust by direct trace: single shared gate (assertActivePtClientRelationship), clientId always from URL path never request body, re-verified fresh fail-closed on every call, across all 10 coach.controller.ts handlers including program assignment and CycleAssessment review (both nutrition and training side)

AI never autonomously messages a client or writes to a client's plan without an explicit human action; every ai-service tool acts only on the calling user's own account, the one PT-facing AI-generation surface (generatePlanDraft) is confirmed draft-only

resolved_questions.question: Exact mechanics of client+pt dual-capability account
resolved_questions.answer: Role is a single mutually-exclusive enum column (not multi-role); functional dual-capability exists because ownership checks use userId, not role. Confirmed by direct trace, see 08-pt-client-management-ai-copilot-audit.md section 4.

resolved_questions.question: Whether a PT can reach another PT's client data by supplying a clientId without a server-side relationship check
resolved_questions.answer: No. Confirmed: clientId source is always the URL path across all 10 coach.controller.ts handlers, never the request body; relationship re-verified fresh, fail-closed, on every call. See section 1 of the same file.
